title: GEMS: Molecular Structure Elucidation as Learned Search over Isomer Graphs
abstract: arXiv:2610.23617v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Identifying small-molecule structures from molecular formulas and tandem mass spectra remains a bottleneck in untargeted metabolomics and natural-product discovery. Even when database retrieval or de novo prediction misses the exact structure, the resulting candidates can provide starting points for exploring nearby structures through a few bond edits. We introduce GEMS (Guided Editing of Molecular Structures), which refines candidates through learned 2-switch bond edits that preserve the molecular formula and each atom's total valence. GEMS uses MIST, a pretrained spectrum-to-fingerprint model, to predict fingerprint probabilities once per spectrum. A neural policy compares each candidate's fingerprint with these predictions, links present features to the atoms and bonds that generate them, and scores all valid edits in one forward pass. The policy is trained on shortest edit paths between structures, so it can be pretrained on PubChem

translated_title: GEMS：将分子结构解析视为同分异构图上的学习式搜索
translated_abstract: 从分子式和串联质谱中鉴定小分子结构，仍然是非靶向代谢组学和天然产物发现中的一个瓶颈。即使数据库检索或从头预测无法命中确切结构，所得到的候选物也可以作为起点，通过少量键编辑来探索其邻近的结构。我们提出GEMS（分子结构引导编辑，Guided Editing of Molecular Structures），它通过学习到的2-switch键编辑来精炼候选结构，这些编辑保持分子式以及每个原子的总化合价不变。GEMS使用MIST——一个预训练的“谱图到分子指纹”模型——对每张谱图一次性预测指纹概率。神经策略将每个候选物的指纹与这些预测进行比较，将存在的特征与其生成的原子和键关联起来，并在一次前向传播中对所有有效编辑进行评分。该策略在结构之间的最短编辑路径上训练，因此可以在PubChem上进行预训练。
tldr: 提出GEMS方法，通过学习保持分子式和原子化合价不变的2-switch键编辑操作来精炼候选分子结构，并借助预训练谱图-指纹模型MIST与神经策略在单次前向传播中评分所有有效编辑，从而解决从分子式和串联质谱解析小分子结构的难题。
